newsitem.title: UK: UK output prices up 0.2% in January.
newsitem.headline: UK output prices up 0.2% in January.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) released the following provisional data on UK input and output prices in January.(Prev data in brackets)
INPUT PRICES EX F, D, T, P (unadj)
INPUT PRICES EX F, D, T, P (adj)
INPUT COMPONENTS PCT CHANGE JAN M/M JAN Y/Y

Consensus of economists forecasts was for input prices to fall a seasonally adjusted 0.1 percent in January and fall 5.6 percent year-on-year. Unadjusted output prices are forecast up 0.4 percent and 1.7 percent higher year-on-year.
* The ONS said the 1.5 percent year-on-year rise in output prices was the lowest rate of increase since October 1986.
The output price index excluding food, beverages, tobacco and petroleum, up 0.6 percent, showed the lowest rate of increase since August 1967.
A 1.0 percent year-on-year increase in food products and beverages was the lowest rise since before 1975.
The ONS said there was little sign of petroleum prices increasing, suggesting measures introduced in last November's budget have not been entirely passed on to consumers.
Output prices excluding excise duties rose 1.0 percent year-on-year, the lowest rate of increase since October 1986.
The weakness in input prices reflected widespread falls in the prices of imported commodities.
